A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same NAMMD research, with matching title, authors, and principal method. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables, and figures, support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original DCT and two-sample testing experiments on five benchmark datasets, ImageNet variants, and adversarially perturbed CIFAR10, with additional appendix analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and adds empirical NAMMD saturation values and runtime comparisons in Tables 3 and 7.

M1.justification: The NAMMD statistic, Gaussian-threshold DCT procedure, permutation-based two-sample test, kernel optimization, and NAMMDFuse remain unchanged. Appendix B.2 details the unequal-sample extension already described in v1's sample-size footnote; it does not establish a revision to the existing method.

E1.justification: V2 adds an extreme-concentration scenario using Gaussian distributions centered at -1000 and 1000 with progressively smaller variances (Appendix B.1). The benchmark datasets, ImageNet scenarios, and CIFAR10 adversarial evaluation remain covered.

E2.justification: The DCT comparisons retain Canonne's test and MMD. The six two-sample comparators remain MMDFuse, MMD-D, MMDAgg, AutoTST, MEMaBiD, and ACTT; the new runtime table uses this existing comparator set.

E3.justification: New evaluations include a Gaussian concentration sweep with bandwidth 1 and sigma ranging from 1 to 10^-8, and runtime measurements in seconds for sample sizes 50–400. The retained experiments' stated training, testing, and data-construction protocols are unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix B.1 adds a sensitivity analysis testing whether NAMMD approaches 1 as separated Gaussians become concentrated. V1's calibrated Gaussian example supporting the TST power theorem is removed. Existing sample-structure, kernel-selection, and type-I-error analyses remain.

E5.justification: Removing v1 Appendix B.2 also removes its disclosure of 1,000 runs with 10,000 samples each for estimating the TST threshold and variance. Repetition counts and mean±standard-deviation reporting for retained experiments are unchanged; the new tables add no uncertainty quantification.

E6.justification: V2 adds saturation results, including NAMMD 0.2679 at sigma=1 and 1 at sigma=10^-8, and runtime results: at 200 samples, NAMMDFuse takes 14.388 seconds versus MMDFuse's 14.015 seconds. V1's TST calibration example disappears. Matched benchmark tables and plotted results are unchanged.

T1.justification: V2 removes substantial TST theory, including Theorems 10–12, the explicit null-distribution result, permutation concentration bound, and associated proofs. It adds formal unequal-sample estimation and saturation conditions while largely retaining DCT guarantees. Its expanded MMD identity in Section 2 incorrectly adds the inner product instead of subtracting twice it.

C1.justification: V1's abstract and introduction claim theoretically and empirically superior NAMMD-based two-sample testing. V2 withdraws that theoretical contribution and emphasizes DCT guarantees. Two-sample testing remains an empirical application and is still mentioned in the conclusion.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly emphasizes the asymptotic scope of the DCT power comparison and adds an interpretation of the runtime results as showing minimal computational overhead. It further explains saturation behavior and concentration in RKHS. The substantive kernel-family limitations are retained.

D1.justification: V2 discloses precomputing pairwise kernel quantities and reusing them through index rearrangement during permutations, and explicitly documents unequal-sample estimation. These are additional implementation details, not demonstrated changes to execution. The code-access information remains unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds Lee's U-statistics: Theory and Practice (2019) for unequal-sample estimation. The covariance-based research positioning moves from v1 Appendix C.4 into Section 3. Correcting Papoulis's name and removing a duplicate Ben-David reference are bibliographic cleanup.

P1.justification: V2 substantially reorganizes the narrative: the dedicated TST section becomes a shorter discussion within Section 3, variance and concentration lemmas move into the main theory section, and the appendices are restructured. The preliminaries are rewritten around general distance-based DCT, and limitations become a separate appendix.

P2.justification: V2 removes the two notation tables and adds saturation and runtime tables. Figure 1(c–d) uses a narrower p-value axis without changing the underlying values. Existing appendix figures and result tables are relocated and renumbered; their substantive displays remain largely unchanged.

improvement.justification: V2 provides clearer organization, explicit unequal-sample details, and useful saturation and runtime evidence. However, it withdraws a substantial TST theoretical contribution while narrowing its claims, and introduces an incorrect MMD expansion in Section 2. These documentation gains and changes to mathematical content do not establish a reliably assessable net improvement or deterioration.
